findings.claim: Read-only guarantee is overstated: managed settings and --settings hooks can still write, so WriteDisabled=true on init evidence alone is unsound.
findings.trigger: Machine with a managed Claude Code hook that writes on session start reviews a consultation.

evidence.observation: Design admits managed settings and --settings still apply under --restricted, so a managed hook could write.
Init tool list cannot prove hooks absent; tree-check plus init check is detection, not prevention.

findings.verification: Install a managed write-hook in scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and run a restricted turn; check tree and hook log.
findings.remedy: Downgrade invariant to detected-not-prevented; add --settings /dev/null equivalent if CLI supports it, document managed-hook residual risk, keep tree-check warn path.

findings.claim: Child environment scrub list is assumed and incomplete; ANTHROPIC_* wildcard plus named Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry vars may miss model/base-url overrides and leaks subscription identity.
findings.trigger: Operator exports a new ANTHROPIC_MODEL or CLAUDE_CODE_* override not on the list.

evidence.observation: Brief marks the variable names assumed and keeps CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for login.
Allowlist-keep of config dir plus denylist-remove of env is fail-open to new variable names.

findings.verification: Dump child env names in fake-claude ARGV_LOG run and diff against scrub list.
findings.remedy: Enumerate env from a live probe, switch to denylist generated from `claude --help`/docs plus fail-closed test that child env names are logged and diffed.

findings.claim: Roster validator and telemetry patterns are inconsistent and the context-token table is assumed; alias-float plus [1m] suffix handling risks mismatch between sent, resolved, and logged models.
findings.trigger: Roster uses claude-opus-5-5[1m] or a future alias; telemetry buckets it as other or guard misroutes.

evidence.observation: Validator regex contains a literal [1m] alternative and open claude-* suffix; context tokens marked assumed per model.

findings.verification: Unit-test validator/telemetry against alias, full id, [1m], and unknown claude-* inputs.
findings.remedy: Normalize-then-validate (strip [1m] first), pin validator to tested id list, source context tokens from observed init or mark unknown instead of assumed values.

findings.claim: Concurrent claude panel members plus coordinator share ~/.claude state with no serialization; Q12 is load-bearing and verification covers only one reviewer.
findings.trigger: Panel runs two claude children concurrently on one host.

evidence.observation: Q12 explicitly open; transcripts share projectsDirectory beside operator sessions; verification is a single reviewer plus one resume.

findings.verification: Run two concurrent claude turns plus coordinator load and check transcripts, exit codes, and ~/.claude.json integrity.
findings.remedy: Default panel to serial claude members (or one claude per panel) until a two-child stress run proves ~/.claude.json safety; record the gate in Get-PanelPlan.

findings.claim: Denial, quota, and resume semantics are undefined: dontAsk denial shape, rate_limit_event payload, exit/subtype taxonomy, stdin upper bound, and resume-after-kill id are all assumed, so classifiers may mislabel empty success as usable.
findings.trigger: Read outside workdir, quota hit, 200KB brief, or taskkill mid-tool_use on a live turn.

evidence.observation: Q2,Q5,Q6,Q7,Q10,Q11 and Q1-upper-bound all open; DeniedEmpty fires only on evidence and repair resumes the minted thread unconditionally.

findings.verification: Execute Requested checks 1-4 in the brief and capture full stream, subtype, denials, exit code, and resumed session_id.
findings.remedy: Ship with fail-closed mapping table (unknown subtype/exit -> transient, unknown denial shape -> permission investigation), require thread-id equality on resume, cap stdin with chunking until 200KB probe passes.

findings.claim: Setting WriteDisabled=true based on the init tool list cannot justify attributing all tree changes to someone other than the reviewer when managed hooks can still execute.
findings.trigger: An applicable managed hook writes to the repository while init reports only the permitted tools, no MCP servers, and dontAsk.

evidence.observation: The design explicitly acknowledges managed-hook writes, then proposes WriteDisabled=true and warning-only tree changes.
Get-EngineTreeCheck uses WriteDisabled to produce the assertion that the change is not the reviewer's.

evidence.reference: Proposed init checks and existing Get-EngineTreeCheck
evidence.observation: Tool inventory does not establish that the surrounding CLI process and its hooks cannot write; post-start validation also cannot prevent earlier hook effects.

findings.verification: In an isolated test installation, configure a managed hook to write a sentinel in a disposable repository and run the proposed restricted argv; compare the sentinel with the accepted init fields.
findings.remedy: Separate model-tool restrictions from process write prevention. Keep WriteDisabled=false unless hook execution is excluded or OS isolation prevents repository writes; preserve unattributed tree changes as failures under the strict read-only contract.

findings.claim: The api-key mode does not exclude inherited gateway routing or competing credentials, despite declaring non-Anthropic routes out of scope.
findings.trigger: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present alongside ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or a third-party provider selector.

evidence.observation: The environment scrub is specified for subscription mode; api-key mode only requires and passes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, while gateway and third-party routes are excluded from scope.
The [environment reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) documents ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL as an endpoint override.

findings.verification: Launch a fake child in api-key mode with a dummy key, loopback base URL and provider selectors; inspect its environment and the resulting provider identity without sending a real request.
findings.remedy: Define explicit environment policies for both auth modes. In api-key mode retain the selected key while removing or refusing conflicting auth and routing settings; verify the effective provider and credential source.

findings.claim: A ChildEnv hook applied only at turn launch leaves authentication preflight observing a different environment from the actual reviewer.
findings.trigger: The parent contains an API key or provider override that the subscription turn removes.

evidence.observation: The proposed hook is described inside the turn-launch transaction; the auth-status preflight has no corresponding effective-environment requirement.
Start-ProbeProcess uses a separate ProcessStartInfo path that removes host markers and test variables, not the proposed adapter environment.
Preflight can reject a valid subscription because it sees an inherited API credential, or record provider metadata that does not describe execution.

findings.verification: Use a fake auth-status executable and fake reviewer to record environment names for the same subscription entry with an inherited dummy API key; require identical effective auth and routing policy.
findings.remedy: Apply one engine environment builder to preflight, version probes and every turn, including repair and continuation; preserve transactional restoration on all paths.

findings.claim: Inherited CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY can disable persistence even though the adapter omits --no-session-persistence, breaking repair and continuation.

evidence.observation: The host-marker scrub uses exact Claude variable names and does not include CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY; the proposed additional scrub does not include it either.
The [CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference) identifies this variable as disabling persistence.

findings.verification: Run a disposable new session with the variable enabled, then attempt resume using its reported UUID; repeat after the adapter removes it.
findings.remedy: Remove the variable for this persistent engine and verify transcript durability before treating a killed session as resumable.

findings.claim: The proposed scrub leaves CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL intact, allowing inherited effort to override both the requested review effort and low-effort repair.
findings.trigger: The parent sets CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL to a value different from --effort.

evidence.observation: The existing scrub removes CLAUDE_EFFORT, a different name; neither the existing list nor the proposed additions removes CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL.
The [environment reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) states that CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL takes precedence over --effort.

findings.verification: Set CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=max in the harness parent and verify that a fake repair child receives --effort low without the conflicting variable.
findings.remedy: Remove the inherited effort variable in both auth modes and record requested effort separately from confirmed or unknown effective effort.

findings.claim: Comparing only init.model cannot enforce the invariant that a thread uses one resolved model throughout the turn.
findings.trigger: The CLI switches the primary model after init through a configured or automatic fallback.

evidence.observation: The design validates model identity at init and records modelUsage keys without specifying subsequent drift enforcement.
The [model documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config) describes within-turn fallback and category-based switching that can persist for the session.

evidence.reference: Init-only validation versus subsequent model switching
evidence.observation: A matching initial model does not establish the identity of the model that produced the accepted reply.

findings.verification: Feed the adapter a stream with matching init.model followed by a primary-model fallback event and a successful answer from another model; require a capability failure.
findings.remedy: Validate primary assistant model identities and explicit fallback events throughout the stream. Corroborate with modelUsage while distinguishing auxiliary requests; refuse continuation on a contaminated lineage.

findings.claim: One engine-wide health bucket conflates independent API and subscription credentials and model-specific subscription limits.
findings.trigger: A subscription Opus-specific quota is exhausted while Sonnet or the separately configured API-key route remains available.

evidence.observation: The design supports two auth mechanisms but makes all claude labels share engine health on the premise of one plan.
The [published types](https://app.unpkg.com/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.185/files/sdk.d.ts) distinguish shared and model-specific rateLimitType values and overage state.

findings.verification: Replay an Opus-specific rejected subscription event, then evaluate eligibility of Sonnet on that subscription and a separate API-key entry; neither should be excluded solely by the Opus bucket.
findings.remedy: Key health by credential/auth scope and reported quota bucket, with explicit handling for genuinely account-wide limits and unknown scope; do not store credential secrets in the ledger.

findings.claim: The stated reason for refusing MaxModelSteps is incorrect: absence from --help does not establish that --max-turns is unsupported.
findings.trigger: An operator requests an agentic-turn limit.

evidence.observation: The proposal explicitly derives StepsFlag='' from the flag's absence in help.
The [CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference) documents --max-turns for print mode and warns that help omits flags.

findings.verification: On CLI 2.1.285, run a disposable task requiring successive tool turns with --max-turns 1 and capture the terminal subtype and exit code.
findings.remedy: Capability-test the supported version and map MaxModelSteps if its semantics fit; otherwise document a deliberate semantic limitation rather than claiming the flag is unavailable.

findings.claim: The preflight rules conflict for a normal signed-out response: loggedIn=false means out, but every nonzero exit means not checked.
findings.trigger: claude auth status returns valid signed-out JSON with exit code 1.

evidence.observation: Both classifications are specified without precedence.
The [CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference) specifies exit 1 when signed out.

findings.verification: Provide the preflight parser valid JSON containing loggedIn=false with exit code 1 and require status out.
findings.remedy: Recognize documented exit-code/JSON combinations first; reserve not checked for malformed, unexpected, unsupported or timed-out responses.

findings.claim: Parallel instances of the claude engine sharing the same global state directory (~/.claude) will encounter race conditions during config or transcript writes.
findings.trigger: Running multiple claude engines concurrently in a panel without isolated config directories.

evidence.observation: Concurrent CLI processes modifying the same JSON configuration file will lead to corruption or locked file errors.

findings.verification: Run two parallel instances of `claude -p` and monitor file access errors on `~/.claude.json`.
findings.remedy: Isolate the global state by setting a unique `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable for each claude engine instance.

findings.claim: A hard-killed session transcript may become corrupted, preventing successful resumes.
findings.trigger: Killing the claude process with taskkill /F mid-turn.

evidence.reference: Design section on timeouts and kills
evidence.observation: Appending JSON objects to a file might be interrupted, leaving malformed JSON at the end of the transcript.

findings.verification: Kill a session mid-thinking and attempt to `--resume` it.
findings.remedy: Implement a salvage script that sanitizes the last line of the transcript file before attempting a resume.

ratings.note: two findings, both generic; the concurrency point was raised more precisely by another reviewer
